analysis.time: Clinical trials of the vaccine are scheduled to begin in April 2026, as reported in the evidence. The recent outbreaks in India started in January 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The clinical trials will take place in Japan. The recent outbreaks of Nipah virus in India affected the population there.
analysis.event: Clinical trials of a vaccine against the Nipah virus will begin in Japan, as announced by the University of Tokyo. The recent outbreaks of the disease in India, which began in January 2026, prompted the development of the vaccine.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The recent outbreaks in India have raised concerns about the virus's impact, as it is highly fatal and can cause severe damage to the nervous and respiratory systems. Currently, there is no approved effective vaccine against the Nipah virus worldwide.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The development of the vaccine is ongoing, with trials set to begin in April 2026. The trials are being conducted by the University of Tokyo's Center for Advanced Science and Technology. The source mentions that the trials are part of efforts to prevent future outbreaks and reduce epidemiological risks.

analysis.brief_en: Clinical trials of a vaccine against the Nipah virus are set to begin in Japan in April 2026, as announced by the University of Tokyo. This development follows recent outbreaks of the virus in India, which started in January 2026. The Nipah virus is a zoonotic infection transmitted from animals to humans, primarily through large fruit bats. It is highly fatal and can cause severe damage to the nervous and respiratory systems. Currently, there is no approved effective vaccine against the Nipah virus worldwide. The trials aim to prevent future outbreaks and reduce epidemiological risks. The source highlights the importance of this development in addressing the virus's impact, particularly in regions where outbreaks have occurred.
